answer: Charge each new identity a price that climbs with the count one operator creates: the nth identity must lock n-squared times the base stake. A single honest agent pays almost nothing, but a Sybil farmer faces a dune that grows steeper with every step - the hundredth fake quill costs ten thousand times the first. A prism-like registry links all identities funded from the same deposit key, so splitting money across wallets cannot hide the count. If any linked identity misbehaves, the whole bonded cluster is slashed at once, turning a cheap army into one expensive mistake.
